extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: CommonCatalog is an open dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model. The paper describes CommonCatalog as containing roughly 70 million open-licensed CC images, with commercial and non-commercial splits, created to train the CommonCanvas text-to-image models.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan; A. Feder Cooper; Jasmine Collins; Landan Seguin; Austin Jacobson; Mihir Patel; Jonathan Frankle; Cory Stephenson; Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by starting from the YFCC100M dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files, then re-scraping the images from Flickr using the Flickr IDs in the YFCC100M metadata, excluding non-derivative licenses, and organizing the remaining images into commercial and non-commercial subsets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: CC images rarely have the alt-text captions necessary to train a T2I model; those that do have associated text often just include the image title or a URL.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YFCC100M Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs linking to the original data; re-scraped high-resolution images from Flickr based on the YFCC100M metadata.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated for Creative-Commons images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B image-captioning model after center-cropping and resizing images to a maximum of 512x512 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors compared several captioning models and, based on qualitative analysis and state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO, chose the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model for synthesizing captions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: CommonCatalog is limited to roughly 70 million usable CC images, far fewer than LAION; CC images rarely have the captions necessary to train a T2I model and associated text often just includes the image title or a URL; synthetic captions have reduced caption diversity and reduced diversity of n-grams; the model underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings; the YFCC100M data is about a decade old, so its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work is motivated by copyright and reproducibility concerns with web-scraped datasets like LAION; the authors state that directly sourcing and distributing CC-licensed images with known provenance could avoid some copyright concerns and solve link rot, enabling greater reproducibility; they also note that adversarial prompts can still produce content including iconic characters, though their model deviated more from such characters than SD2
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains Creative-Commons images, including images of individual people and some noteworthy public figures/celebrities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: training text-to-image generative models; training and evaluating open diffusion/text-to-image models using Creative-Commons images and synthetic captions
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: They use a pre-trained BLIP-2 model to produce synthetic captions for otherwise uncaptioned Creative-Commons images, creating synthetic image-caption pairs for training.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: They re-scraped images from Flickr based on YFCC100M IDs, excluded images with non-derivative licenses, and for caption generation center-cropped and resized all images to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels.
